payload.headline: Tesla trades near the top of its own history while profits shrink

summary.thesis: Tesla has a strong balance sheet, but the 390.84 price needs far faster growth than the shrinking margins and cash flow now show.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just under resistance with no clear trend.
summary.act_at: Revisit near 203.8 on value; watch 380.15–400.51 for the trading range

payload.happening: TSLA closed at 390.84, up 2.91% on the day. That puts it just under a resistance band at 393.63–400.51 and near its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (381.83, 373.65, 383.03), which are all flat, so the stock is moving sideways. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The latest quarter (ended 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-22) weakened the business. Quarterly sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, down from 15.78% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, slipped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending, halved to 3.3B from 6.8B. Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0% (both against a year earlier). That gap can force price cuts and squeeze margins again. The quality grade is D. Not at risk is the balance sheet: 17.9B cash against 8.0B debt, 37.5B net cash and 45.4B total liquidity, so funding stress is not the issue. Share dilution is small at 0.43% a year. The rally to 390.84 reflects sentiment more than results. Segment data is not available, so this note cannot say which product lines drive the slowdown.

worth.text: The two valuation methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow valuation (DCF) starts from 3.3B of trailing free cash flow and a 9.9% discount rate. It gives 20.23 (bear), 25.02 (base) and 45.34 (bull) per share. Even with 30% starting growth it reaches only 45.55, and if operating margin falls to 1% it drops to 21.83. The second method asks what the stock would be worth at its usual price-to-sales ratios over the past 5 years, and gives 203.8 to 399.81. The price is 430.1 times trailing earnings and 14.9 times sales, at the 77th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. The data estimates that the price needs about 51% a year growth, while sales grew 3% a year over 3 years and 8% over the last 12 months. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: whether investors keep paying a high sales multiple for growth the cash flows do not yet show. My range uses the history-based values. The cash-flow values sit far below them.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on current free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: 37.5B net cash and 45.4B liquidity give room to invest through a slow patch.
Trailing sales still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts' next-year EPS growth is 25%.
The price sits above its 50-day average of 373.65, with heavy support at 380.15–389.95 (11 touches).
bear: The price is 430.1 times trailing earnings, and every cash-flow value is at or below 45.34 per share.
Free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, and operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which signals possible price cuts ahead.

levels.what: The current close, near the top of the history-based range and far above every cash-flow value.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above this, even the generous method calls the stock expensive.
The low end of the own-history range, where the price would start to reflect slower growth.

longterm.why: This is a grade D business with falling margins and cash flow, priced near the top of its own valuation history. The rules committee also says Avoid.

swing.why: The stock is in a sideways range, just under resistance at 393.63–400.51 and above support at 380.15–389.95. The room to the next ceiling is small next to the 16.61 average daily range. A clear close above 400.51 or a pullback into support would give a better setup.

decision.timing: Earnings come out on 2027-01-27, after the 2027-01-15 options expiry. Options price only about a 5.5% move by 2026-11-20 (implied volatility 42.5 vs realized 61.3), so the big catalyst is the January report, not the coming weeks.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and the inventory build easing against sales.
Trailing free cash flow recovers toward 6.8B, which would lift the cash-flow values from the 20.23–45.34 range.
A close below the 364.02–368.6 support zone would confirm weakness, and a close above 417.44 would break the range upward.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
